claims.text: The initial FeCoNi alloy is single-phase fcc.
The initial single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy has high saturation magnetization.
The initial alloy has a coercive field of approximately 100 Oe.
Aging FeCoNi at approximately 500 °C for 2–4 hours with controlled cooling will form nanoscale coherent precipitates in the fcc matrix.
The aging treatment can produce a slight lattice mismatch between the nanoprecipitates and the fcc matrix.
Controlled cooling will lock in the nanoprecipitate structure.
The precipitates will be distributed uniformly within the fcc matrix.
Slightly mismatched coherent nanoprecipitates generate localized lattice strain or distortion.
The precipitate-induced lattice distortions increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The coherent nanoprecipitates act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain-wall pinning hinder domain-wall motion and raise coercivity.
The aging treatment will increase the coercive field beyond 100 Oe relative to untreated FeCoNi.
The aged alloy will largely retain the high saturation magnetization of the untreated fcc FeCoNi alloy.
The aging process can form the proposed precipitates without causing an unwanted phase transformation or carbide formation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires formation of nanoprecipitates while also requiring retention of a single-phase, phase-pure fcc alloy and treating secondary-phase formation as an adverse outcome. Unless the precipitates are explicitly defined as coherent compositional fluctuations within one thermodynamic phase, precipitate formation implies phase separation and conflicts with the single-phase boundary.
